findings.name: shadcn/ui (CLI, registries, MCP server, skill)
findings.what_it_does: Copy-in React components (Base UI, React Aria or Radix, plus Tailwind) installed by a CLI and registries. Ships an MCP server and a Claude-readable skill. Since July 2026 'shadcn init' defaults to Base UI; '-b radix' selects Radix.
findings.how_we_use_it: Run 'shadcn init -t vite -b base', record the base in CLAUDE.md, then 'mcp init --client claude' and 'skills add shadcn/ui' so Claude installs canonical components. Theme with our tokens. Tell Claude to use the render prop, not asChild.
findings.saves: Canonical code from CLI and MCP means fewer fix-up loops and tokens; the default path keeps docs, skill and examples aligned.
findings.risks: Copied code becomes ours to maintain. Default look is generic without custom tokens. Base UI and Radix snippets differ (render vs asChild), so mixed examples break. Needs Node and pnpm, not installed yet.

findings.name: Base UI (new shadcn default) and Radix Primitives
findings.what_it_does: Unstyled accessible React components from the creators of Radix, Floating UI and MUI; MIT; npm @base-ui/react 1.9.0 (9 Oct 2026). Radix Primitives (WorkOS, MIT) stays supported and is used only when shadcn is initialised with -b radix.
findings.how_we_use_it: Consume through shadcn only; import directly just for custom widgets such as port popovers. Choose once and write it into PRODUCT.md and CLAUDE.md. Fall back to '-b radix' if a needed component is missing; shadcn's migration skill converts components later.
findings.maintainer: MUI and Base UI team (Radix: WorkOS)
findings.last_activity: Base UI pushed 2026-10-21, v1.9.0 on 2026-10-09; Radix primitives pushed 2026-10-14
findings.popularity: Base UI 11.2k stars, 298 open issues plus 133 PRs; Radix 19.4k stars
findings.saves: Focus, keyboard and ARIA behaviour for overlays and menus come prebuilt; following shadcn's default avoids doc and skill mismatches.
findings.risks: Younger than Radix, with fewer community snippets, so model habits (asChild) may mislead. Not tested here with our canvas popovers. React Flow UI registry items import no Radix directly (11 checked), so either base works.

findings.name: Tailwind CSS (v4, CSS-first)
findings.what_it_does: Utility-first CSS framework. Version 4 declares theme tokens as CSS variables in an @theme block instead of tailwind.config.js. Current npm release 4.3.3 (16 Jul 2026). shadcn and React Flow UI assume it.
findings.how_we_use_it: Tokens emit CSS custom properties that an '@theme inline' block references, so utilities follow theme switches. Light/dark via a data attribute on the root. Pin 4.3.x. Give Claude no tailwind.config.js guidance.
findings.saves: Compact class strings cost fewer tokens than bespoke CSS and keep generated UI consistent.
findings.risks: Long class lists hurt readability; token discipline needed. Data-attribute dark-mode syntax was not read (theme page only links it). React Flow's stylesheet must import after Tailwind.

findings.name: React Flow (xyflow)
findings.what_it_does: MIT library for node-based UIs: custom nodes, handles, edges, minimap. Docs: Tab focuses nodes and edges, Enter/Space selects, arrows move nodes, Delete removes edges, assertive live region. connectOnClick (default true) allows click-click wiring. No documented keyboard edge creation.
findings.how_we_use_it: Canvas engine, @xyflow/react 12.12.x. Custom node cards per category; typed ports via isValidConnection. We build a keyboard 'Connect...' command and an Edges list. dagre for Tidy. Test onlyRenderVisibleElements (default false) on large graphs.
findings.saves: Avoids building pan/zoom, selection, wiring, minimap and focus plumbing from scratch.
findings.risks: Keyboard wiring is ours to build (WCAG 2.1.1). Valid/invalid target styling is custom CSS. Large graphs need memoisation. Keep our graph JSON independent of React Flow's node shape.

findings.name: React Flow UI (shadcn-based components; templates are Pro)
findings.what_it_does: Components for React Flow installed from a shadcn-style registry: base node, handles, status indicator, node search, zoom slider, devtools. Needs React 19 and Tailwind 4. Both templates are labelled Pro examples; Pro starts at $169 per month.
findings.how_we_use_it: Do not build on the templates. Read the component sources as references (11 checked import no Radix package, only React, @xyflow/react, lucide and shadcn parts). Vendor one only after xyflow confirms its licence; otherwise rewrite, since each file is short.
findings.license: Not stated per component; site footer links xyflow's MIT; registry files carry no licence header
findings.saves: Study of finished, token-ready node, handle and status parts saves days of node-card design even if we rewrite them.
findings.risks: Component licence unresolved. Templates need paid Pro and use Next.js, ELKjs and Zustand. Strict stylesheet import order. Newer, opinionated, few external references.

findings.name: cmdk (with kbar and React Aria fallbacks)
findings.what_it_does: Unstyled React command-menu component with filtering, keyword aliases and a dialog wrapper. shadcn's Command wraps it. npm 1.1.1 (14 Mar 2025) accepts React 18 or 19. Good to roughly 2-3k items.
findings.how_we_use_it: Ctrl/Cmd+K palette via shadcn Command, wrapped in our own Palette component so it can swap to kbar (timc1/kbar, MIT, npm 1.0.0, 10 Aug 2026) or React Aria's combobox (shadcn offers an aria base). Modules register commands, including 'Connect...'.
findings.saves: Fuzzy matching, keyboard handling and dialog wiring done; one CLI call to add.
findings.risks: Dormant: no release since March 2025, 76 open issues. React 19 is supported (earlier note was wrong). No virtualisation. Wrapping it keeps the swap cheap. React Aria is a second primitives set.

findings.name: react-resizable-panels (and dockview later)
findings.what_it_does: MIT React components for resizable, collapsible panel layouts with keyboard-friendly separators and layout save/restore. shadcn's Resizable wraps it. dockview (MIT core, 8.6.1 on 19 Oct 2026; enterprise package proprietary) adds tabbed docking.
findings.how_we_use_it: App shell: phase rail left, canvas centre, inspector and sources right. Collapse everything for Present mode and persist layout per phase. Keep dockview for later pop-out and tabbed docking.
findings.saves: Resizable, collapsible, persisted panels without custom drag code.
findings.risks: Single maintainer. API changed between versions. No tabbed docking or pop-outs; dockview is the upgrade but its enterprise package is proprietary.

findings.name: Impeccable (design skill, 24 commands, detector)
findings.what_it_does: Design skill for AI coding agents: 24 commands (critique, audit, polish, onboard, animate and more) and 61 deterministic rules that flag AI-looking UI without an LLM. The installer downloads an engine binary and writes agent hooks.
findings.how_we_use_it: Install only after review: use --no-hooks, set DO_NOT_TRACK=1, inspect the binary fetched into ~/.impeccable/bin. Then run critique, audit and polish before demos after 13 Nov. Load at most two design aids per session.
findings.saves: Rule detection costs zero tokens; PRODUCT.md avoids restating the brief each session.
findings.risks: Telemetry on by default; README names no download host; hooks edit .claude/settings.local.json and can trigger the binary fetch. Live mode runs a package.json script. Lists Inter as overused. 24 commands add context.

findings.name: Anthropic frontend-design skill (anthropics/skills)
findings.what_it_does: Short skill steering Claude toward deliberate typography, a named 4-6 colour palette, one orchestrated motion moment, visible focus states, and away from generic rounded SaaS cards and gradient washes.
findings.how_we_use_it: First-pass generation for Present-mode board layouts, landing and community pages after 13 Nov. Combine with our tokens; do not apply its marketing-page flourishes to the dense canvas UI.
findings.license: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE.txt in the skill folder; repo root shows none)
findings.saves: Small single SKILL.md, cheap to load; first drafts need fewer aesthetic revisions.
findings.risks: Targets marketing-style pages, not analysis tools; may push decorative choices against focus goals. Repo licence field is empty, so rely on the per-skill Apache file.

findings.name: Vercel web-design-guidelines skill and Web Interface Guidelines
findings.what_it_does: A skill that reviews UI files against 100+ rules (visible focus, keyboard handlers, reduced motion, transform/opacity-only animation, undo for destructive actions) and prints terse file:line findings. Rules live in an MIT repo.
findings.how_we_use_it: Vendor a pinned copy of command.md into the project and run it on changed UI files before merges, instead of fetching main at review time. Add our canvas-specific rules beside it. It is the default review aid for the 13 Nov core.
findings.license: MIT (README; GitHub API shows no licence field for agent-skills)
findings.saves: Terse file:line output keeps review cost low; replaces writing our own checklist.
findings.risks: The skill fetches rules from GitHub main at run time (reproducibility, injection risk), so vendor and pin. Some rules are Next.js/Vercel-specific. Repo has no LICENSE file.

findings.name: IBM Carbon (design system and data-viz guidance)
findings.what_it_does: Apache-2.0 design system with concrete guidance for data-dense UI: data-viz palettes, chart anatomy, status indicators, notifications, empty states, light/dark tokens. Status pattern pairs colour with shape or symbol and text; warns that more than five or six indicators overwhelm.
findings.how_we_use_it: Reference, not a second component library. Borrow the status rules for Sourced / Team assumption / FALSE ASSUMPTION (colour plus icon plus word), notification persistence, categorical colour order, chart anatomy and empty-state structure.
findings.saves: Tested wording and rules for status, notifications and legends; no research from scratch.
findings.risks: Status page contradicts itself (three elements vs two) and sets no hard cap. Chart page says nothing on number formatting. Mixing Carbon components with shadcn gives two visual languages.

findings.name: Scientific colour maps (Crameri) and cmcrameri
findings.what_it_does: Perceptually uniform, colour-vision-deficiency-friendly maps that stay readable in black and white. Zenodo record 8.0.1 (5 Oct 2023, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8409685) states the MIT licence. cmcrameri is the MIT Python wrapper.
findings.how_we_use_it: Default sequential and diverging ramps for sun, shadow, wind and energy. Export colour stops as JSON with the MIT notice; draw legends from the same stops; cite Crameri et al. 2020 and the DOI in the sources panel. Check ramp ends against the FALSE ASSUMPTION hue.
findings.saves: Avoids designing and testing colour ramps; citable for the sources panel.
findings.risks: JavaScript packaging not verified (zip is 66.9 MB; contents not listed on the page). Categorical maps are limited. Some diverging maps may end near the reserved magenta.

findings.name: Culori (and Radix Colors as alternative)
findings.what_it_does: MIT JavaScript colour library: CSS Color 4 spaces including OKLCH, conversion, interpolation, colour-difference formulas. Radix Colors (MIT, 1.7k stars, pushed 2025-12-17) is a ready-made light/dark scale set.
findings.how_we_use_it: Generate neutral, accent and status scales in OKLCH from three inputs (base, accent, contrast), interpolate legend stops, and check contrast ratios in CI. One-hour spike against Radix Colors, then pick one source only.
findings.saves: Programmatic palettes cut manual colour iteration and keep light/dark themes consistent.
findings.risks: README did not confirm gamut mapping or WCAG contrast helpers. OKLCH lightness is not a contrast guarantee. Two palette sources in parallel would confuse. Small community.

findings.name: Observable Plot (and d3-scale-chromatic fallback)
findings.what_it_does: ISC-licensed concise JavaScript charting from layered marks. Repo docs confirm colour, opacity and symbol legends, ramp or swatch styles, and a standalone Plot.legend(). d3-scale-chromatic (ISC plus Apache-2.0 ColorBrewer) supplies fallback ramps.
findings.how_we_use_it: Chart layer for results panels and SVG board exports. Define one colour scale (fixed domain) per metric, reuse it across compared options, and draw the legend with Plot.legend. Wrap d3-scale-chromatic behind tokens, with ColorBrewer attribution.
findings.saves: Few lines per chart means fewer tokens than hand-written SVG or d3.
findings.risks: Site docs returned HTTP 429; features were read from repo docs. No radius or length legends. Facets and interval marks unverified. d3-scale-chromatic says nothing on colour-blind safety. No 3D.

findings.name: Inter and Geist Mono typefaces
findings.what_it_does: OFL-1.1 fonts. Inter 4.1 (16 Nov 2024) is variable with an opsz axis that provides Display designs. Geist Mono lives in vercel/geist-font, whose fonts/GeistMono folder has variable and webfonts files. The npm geist package targets Next.js.
findings.how_we_use_it: Inter variable with opsz for UI and headings, tabular figures in tables and legends; Geist Mono for IDs, units, citations. Self-host files copied from the repos, with licence notices. Silence Impeccable's overused-font rule for Inter.
findings.popularity: Inter 20k stars; geist-font 3.7k stars, 53 open issues
findings.saves: Two free fonts settle type decisions early; tabular numerals make numeric panels readable.
findings.risks: Inter can read as generic. Geist files must come from the repo, not npm (Next peer dependency). Variable files need subsetting for load time. Geist Mono variable files were listed, not opened or rendered.

findings.name: Motion (motion.dev)
findings.what_it_does: MIT animation library for React, JS and Vue: springs, gestures, layout transitions. MotionConfig reducedMotion='user' disables transform and layout animation while keeping opacity and colour.
findings.how_we_use_it: Panel and phase transitions and node run-state pulses. Wrap the app in MotionConfig reducedMotion='user'. Tokens 100/200/300 ms, 400 ms only for large panel moves; ease-out entering, ease-in leaving; no bounce. Prefer CSS transitions for simple states.
findings.saves: Declarative variants reduce hand-written animation code and review tokens.
findings.risks: Layout animations on a big canvas can cost frames; test. Motion+ paid tier is optional. 'Tiny footprint' claim is unquantified in the README.

findings.name: Playwright MCP, Playwright CLI, Playwright Test and axe-core
findings.what_it_does: Playwright MCP (Apache-2.0) drives a browser via the accessibility tree. @playwright/cli is pre-1.0 (0.1.22, 28 Sep 2026). axe-core (MPL-2.0) finds about 57% of WCAG issues; @axe-core/playwright 4.14.0 runs it in tests.
findings.how_we_use_it: CI: Playwright Test (stable) plus @axe-core/playwright on shell, palette, panels and legends; fail on critical violations. Claude's interactive self-checks use the MCP or pinned CLI: tab through the canvas, screenshot phone and desktop widths, read console errors.
findings.popularity: Playwright MCP 38.4k stars; axe-core 7.7k stars, 444 open issues
findings.saves: Accessibility snapshots avoid vision tokens; axe catches many defects without LLM tokens.
findings.risks: MCP README says it is not a security boundary; one tool runs arbitrary JavaScript. CLI is pre-1.0. axe misses roughly 43% of issues and cannot inspect WebGL. Needs Node 18+, not installed.

findings.name: Style Dictionary and DTCG token format
findings.what_it_does: Apache-2.0 token build tool. npm v5.7.0 released 16 Oct 2026; first-class DTCG ($value/$type) support since v4. Its docs say the 2025.10 DTCG format is not yet fully supported (work in progress for v5).
findings.how_we_use_it: v1 only: author tokens in the DTCG subset v5 supports and emit CSS variables for the '@theme inline' block. For 13 Nov, hand-written CSS variables are enough.
findings.maintainer: Style Dictionary org (DTCG: W3C community group)
findings.saves: A single source of truth stops Claude hard-coding colours; theme changes are one-file edits.
findings.risks: Adds a build step. 2025.10 gaps may require rework. GitHub page showed no release list, so version came from npm. Plain CSS variables may be enough for the whole competition.

findings.name: Rerun (viewer blueprint pattern)
findings.what_it_does: Apache-2.0/MIT multimodal data viewer. Docs: a blueprint is a layer separate from logged data; saved as .rbl files, shared, version-controlled; recordings sharing an Application ID share a blueprint; two resets (heuristic and default).
findings.how_we_use_it: Pattern only: store view layouts (panels, legends, camera, compared set) as shareable JSON apart from model data, keyed to the project. Offer 'auto layout' and 'reset to my default'. Community users fork layouts like modules.
findings.saves: Layout-versus-data separation avoids a later refactor of saved views.
findings.risks: Robotics-focused; its UI toolkit is not ours to reuse. Do not embed the viewer. 1,240 open issues.

findings.name: Speckle viewer (UX benchmark and speckle-server monorepo)
findings.what_it_does: Web viewer with dockable panels: Models, Filters, Views, Issues tabs, an Elements table dock, selection panel with 'add as filter', status-bar undo/redo, shortcut sheet. Saved views capture camera, filters, visibility, sections, measurements. Code: Apache-2.0 unless a folder says otherwise.
findings.how_we_use_it: Copy: Elements table (our 'View as table'), saved views as snapshots, panel shortcuts, layout lock/reset, colour-by-property. Viewer reuse (@speckle/viewer 2.31.14) is a roadmap candidate; coordinate with the viewer packet.
findings.license: Apache-2.0 by default; per-folder exceptions (GitHub shows NOASSERTION)
findings.saves: Reusing patterns, and maybe the viewer, could save weeks of three.js and panel design.
findings.risks: Mixed per-folder licences; Viewer 2 to 3 transition. Docs conflict on who may create views (Editor seat vs Contributor role) and list Views as 'soon'. Legends and themes unverified. Heavy stack.

findings.name: tldraw (SDK and workflow starter kit)
findings.what_it_does: Infinite-canvas React SDK under the tldraw licence: development use free, production use needs a licence key (trial or commercial; pricing page mentions a hobby licence). Starter kits, including a node workflow editor, are MIT.
findings.how_we_use_it: Not a dependency. Read the MIT workflow starter kit for port-bound connections and click-output-to-open-node-picker, then reimplement those ideas on React Flow.
findings.license: tldraw licence (source-available; GitHub reports NOASSERTION); starter kits MIT
findings.saves: Reading the starter kit saves design time for node-picker interactions.
findings.risks: A public deployment is production and needs a key; terms for coursework or open-source competition were not found. Licence mentions usage-data collection. Lock-in.

findings.name: ComfyUI frontend (UX reference only)
findings.what_it_does: Official ComfyUI web UI under GPL-3.0. Docs (re-read) describe a node library sidebar with essentials, search and bookmarks, templates, subgraphs, App Mode and a queue bar. Its litegraph.js base (MIT) is archived.
findings.how_we_use_it: Copy ideas, not code: starter templates, App Mode-style linear view, subgraph collapse and a bookmarkable node library as the beginner on-ramp for our graph.
findings.saves: Studying proven beginner on-ramps saves usability iteration.
findings.risks: GPL-3.0 copyleft would infect our code if copied. 3,056 open issues. Docs page does not describe node error or running states.

findings.name: WCAG 2.2 (W3C Recommendation)
findings.what_it_does: Adds 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured, 2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA), 2.5.8 Target Size (24 px), 3.2.6, 3.3.7, 3.3.8. Understanding pages: 2.1.1 says connect-the-dots wiring needs keyboard access; 1.1.1 wants short plus long alternatives for charts, tables recommended.
findings.how_we_use_it: AA checklist: click-click wiring (2.5.7), keyboard 'Connect...' listbox (2.1.1), Edges list, 'View as table' for viewport analyses (1.1.1), 24 px port targets, panels never fully covering focus, 3:1 for ports, wires and chart marks, colour never sole cue.
findings.saves: Concrete pass/fail criteria prevent late accessibility rework.
findings.risks: Canvas and WebGL content needs custom semantics; automated tools cover only part. Main page read in two chunks (first 100k of 270k characters); Understanding pages read separately.

findings.name: deceptive.design (deceptive pattern types)
findings.what_it_does: Catalogue of 18 deceptive pattern types, including nagging, fake urgency, fake social proof, confirmshaming, addictive design, comparison prevention, hard to cancel, preselection and visual interference.
findings.how_we_use_it: Turn into a PR checklist and a short 'no dark patterns' rule. Apply to notifications, community counters, deadline banners, default selections and any rewards or progress UI.
findings.saves: A ready taxonomy avoids debating each borderline UI choice.
findings.risks: Written mainly for commerce; needs adaptation to an academic community. A checklist, not enforcement.

findings.name: Autodesk Forma (compare and analysis UX benchmark)
findings.what_it_does: Commercial AEC site-design tool. Compare mode shows up to six proposals or analysis results side by side; zoom and pan sync; Inspect on one scene shows point details in every scene; 4K PNG capture. Navigator holds proposals and shared bases.
findings.how_we_use_it: Precedent for our Compare view: named snapshots, linked cameras, linked point inspection, context-sensitive right panel, saved camera views, 'variations as objects'. Cite it in the sources panel. Embodied-carbon page shows scenario data sources and editable values.
findings.saves: A ready, proven compare pattern avoids inventing one and testing it from scratch.
findings.risks: Closed source. autodesk.com tutorial pages return 403; read through a regional mirror and Autodesk blogs. Legends, units and uncertainty are not described in pages read. Unclear whether camera linking can be turned off.

findings.name: Figma UI3 redesign write-up
findings.what_it_does: Figma's account of UI3: canvas focus, resizable collapsible panels, slim bottom toolbar, optional labels, hide-all-UI. Lessons: hover-only UI felt unstable, and some changes were reverted to protect muscle memory. Version history (separate help page) shows autosave checkpoints and named versions.
findings.how_we_use_it: Template for the app shell: stable panel positions, collapse-all for Present mode, optional labels for newcomers, expert shortcuts untouched. Do not move controls between releases without testing. Copy Figma's named-version model for option snapshots.
findings.last_activity: Article undated on the page read; help page read 21 Oct 2026
findings.saves: Proven rationale for layout choices; avoids repeating experiments Figma abandoned.
findings.risks: Different audience (product design). Rollout was gradual with no opt-in beta described. No screenshots were reviewed.

findings.name: Linear redesign write-up (theme generator)
findings.what_it_does: Linear's note on its UI refresh: less sidebar and tab clutter, tighter alignment, themes generated in LCH from three variables (base, accent, contrast), a contrast setting for high-contrast themes, Inter Display headings; shipped behind a feature flag with staged rollout.
findings.how_we_use_it: Model for our token generator: three inputs yield light, dark and high-contrast themes (Culori, OKLCH). Use feature flags and staged rollout for UI changes after 13 Nov. Denser, calmer navigation is the tone target.
findings.last_activity: Article undated on the page read
findings.saves: A tested three-input theme approach avoids hand-tuning dozens of colour variables.
findings.risks: Linear's generator code is not published, so ours is a reimplementation. No contrast measurements shown. Closed commercial product.

findings.name: Spline (benchmark and community remix model)
findings.what_it_does: Browser-based 3D design tool with real-time collaboration and publishing. Its Community Platform lets users publish scenes, repost, comment and remix others' scenes; docs state community files are licensed CC BY 4.0.
findings.how_we_use_it: Benchmark for fork-and-remix: one-click remix of a module into your workspace, attribution preserved, licence shown on each item. Put a licence field in the module manifest. No Spline editor layout is copied.
findings.license: Commercial editor; community files CC BY 4.0 (docs)
findings.saves: Existing remix semantics and licence wording shorten community-feature design.
findings.risks: Editor open-source status unconfirmed (treated as closed). Interface-tour page not opened, so no editor UX claims. A search summary said CC0; the docs say CC BY 4.0. Pricing unchecked.

findings.name: Leva and Tweakpane (parameter-panel spike)
findings.what_it_does: Two MIT GUI-panel libraries for numeric controls. Leva is React-first with 12+ input types and a keyboard-accessible claim (npm 0.10.1, React 18/19). Tweakpane 4.0.5 is vanilla JS (npm and API data only).
findings.how_we_use_it: Half-day spike: compare an inspector built from shadcn form parts with Leva or Tweakpane for scrub plus typed input. Pick one. Numeric input stays beside every slider (WCAG 2.5.7).
findings.popularity: Leva 6.3k stars, 129 open issues; Tweakpane 4.6k stars, 32 open issues
findings.saves: Ready scrubbing inputs for fast preview sliders could save a custom control build.
findings.risks: Leva README is marked heavy development and did not describe scrub or typed input; last release Oct 2025. Tweakpane README not opened. Styling and focus order may clash with our tokens.

findings.name: Vancouver Tall Challenge page, terms and FAQ (Buildner)
findings.what_it_does: Panels are JPEGs up to 10 MB; the brief sets one to four. Judging is anonymous. FAQ: check AI tools' terms; AI images not advised as sole work. Dates: registration 29 Oct, questions 3 Nov, submission 30 Nov 2026.
findings.how_we_use_it: Derive the board export profile (JPEG, size cap, no identifying marks) and AI-image caption rules from these pages. Download the full brief yourselves and confirm panel count, size and AI wording before building Present mode.
findings.maintainer: Buildner with City of Vancouver and UBC SALA
findings.saves: Early constraint knowledge prevents rework of the Present-mode exporter.
findings.risks: Brief PDF sits behind an email form I did not submit, so A2, panel count and any AI rule are unconfirmed. Terms do not mention AI. Registration closes in eight days.

principles.principle: Progressive disclosure, two levels maximum, with the canvas as hero. Show the few controls most users need and reveal the rest on request. Figma's UI3 write-up: canvas focus, resizable collapsible panels, optional labels, hide-all-UI; but hover-only UI made the workspace feel unstable and some moves were reverted to protect muscle memory. Linear cut navigation clutter without changing navigation behaviour. One ComfyUI commenter opposed a hide-nodes Beginner mode (single voice, thin evidence).
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Every module shows an Essentials level plus one Advanced drawer, nothing deeper. Basic -> Advanced -> Present is a persistent phase rail users can jump around, not a locked wizard, because massing, evaluation and design loop back. Panels are resizable and collapsible with layout remembered per phase; Present hides all panels by default; panel positions never move on hover; one inspector open at a time. Essentials modules default on; everything stays searchable in the palette. Counts such as 'seven essentials' are team assumptions.

principles.principle: Protect flow with fast feedback, tiered waits, explicit run states and fixable errors. Flow needs clear goals and immediate feedback. NN/g response-time limits: about 0.1 s feels instant, 1 s keeps thought unbroken, 10 s needs progress and a way out. NN/g heuristics: show system status, support undo, name the problem and suggest a fix. React Flow UI's status indicator already models loading, success, error and initial states. The CHI 2008 interruption study could not be read, so interruption-cost claims are unverified.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Parameter edits show a cheap preview within about 100 ms. Node states: idle, queued, running, stale, failed, warning, done, each as icon plus word. Over 1 s show a busy state on the node; over 10 s show percent, ETA and Cancel, in the background; no modals or focus stealing during runs. Editing an upstream node marks every downstream node 'stale' with an out-of-date label instead of silently recomputing. Error copy names the cause and a fix; a refused wire drop says which type was expected. Performance: memoise node components, collapse large trees, test onlyRenderVisibleElements; a node-count warning (start at 200) is a team assumption.

principles.principle: Wire density is the main readability problem, and wire display is contested. Informal coding of about 25 complaints across four threads: McNeel 48238 (16 posters), McNeel 55455 (23 posters on the page read), a Blender DevTalk UX proposal (18 posters on page one; only the opening post read) and a Hacker News thread (about 15 of 493 comments read). Themes: wire clutter, organisation at scale, surprising implicit behaviour, inconsistent conventions across tools, no text form to diff. In McNeel 48238 the Grasshopper author declined wire-display options for version 2 while at least three posters wanted faint or hidden wires, and four reported creating relays by accident through double-click. Blender's proposal objects to opaque auto-reconnection of occupied sockets and prefers a modifier key. Signals only; Reddit stayed blocked.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Wire modes Full, Faint and Selected-only, one click apart; the default (Full for people reading another team's graph) is decided by the 3-task test. The selected node's wires are always solid. Named Sender/Receiver relays for long runs; creating a relay needs a modifier key, never a bare double-click, since canvas double-click opens search. No implicit reconnection: dropping on an occupied port shows a preview and needs a modifier to replace. Auto-created frames per module category with colour and name, collapse-to-cluster, Tidy via dagre, reroutes that duplicate with their connection, ports with colour, shape and label. One documented shortcut set, since node tools differ in gestures.

principles.principle: Inspect at the wire, preview live, and state units and precision. TouchDesigner docs describe animated wires, interactive node viewers and an info popup; Houdini docs describe flags, status badges and a node-info window. NIST's SI writing rules: a space between number and unit symbol, symbols never pluralised, no more significant digits than the measurement justifies. Carbon's chart pages cover tooltips and KPI numbers but not number formatting. Blender socket inspection remains unverified.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Hover on any port shows value, type, unit, source module and last-run time; every output has 'pin to viewport'. Nodes show a thumbnail or sparkline, run time and warning badge; wire flow animates only during a run. Every value carries an SI unit symbol after a space (for example 12.4 m, 310 kWh/m2). Default 3 significant figures with full precision on hover and copy (team assumption); never show more digits than the least certain input supports; unit conversions are explicit; the rounding policy per metric lives in the module manifest.

principles.principle: Onboard with templates, a linear App view, pulled help and useful empty states. NN/g found tutorials mostly forgotten and recommends help shown on user signal plus a persistent entry point. ComfyUI documents templates, App Mode and subgraphs as its on-ramp (docs re-read). Spline's community teaches by remixing others' scenes. Empty states need status, a learning cue and a direct action.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: By 13 Nov one starter graph on the real Vancouver block; by 10 Dec three (Basic, Advanced, Present). An 'App view' (form plus results) over any graph. Help is pulled (hover '?', first-open hint) with one persistent Help/What's new entry; any tour (optional library Driver.js, MIT) is skippable, re-launchable and never hides focused items (WCAG 2.4.11). Every empty panel has a title, why it is empty, a primary action (import or load sample block) and a docs link; loading never renders as empty. Remixing a community module or graph is the learning route.

principles.principle: Keyboard-first command palette whose shortcuts teach. A good palette opens from anywhere, covers nearly every action, forgives typos, ranks by context and shows shortcuts. Speckle documents Shift+letter panel shortcuts and a cheat sheet; Forma offers a Quick access menu and zoom-to-fit shortcut. The ARIA pattern closest to a palette is an editable combobox with a listbox popup.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Ctrl/Cmd+K toggles the palette and returns focus to its origin. Every action is a command (add node, toggle module, run all, switch phase, open sources, connect ports, export board) with fuzzy search, aliases, context ranking and visible shortcuts; aria-activedescendant on the input. A shortcut cheat sheet is reachable from the palette. The palette component is wrapped so cmdk can be swapped for kbar.

principles.principle: Colour scales and legends must read at a glance. Use perceptually uniform, colour-vision-safe maps (Crameri, MIT per Zenodo); separate sequential from diverging by data meaning; label directly where possible. Colour must not be the only cue (WCAG 1.4.1) and graphics need 3:1 contrast (1.4.11). Carbon: legends explain each visual property, and a data table is the only route to very small slices. Observable Plot draws ramps for continuous scales and swatches for ordinal or threshold scales.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Crameri-style sequential maps by default; a diverging map only when data has a meaningful midpoint; no rainbow; no shipped ramp ends in the FALSE ASSUMPTION hue. Legend always visible on the canvas with units and threshold ticks, drawn from the same colour stops as the shading. Compared options share one scale. Add patterns, labels or values beside colour; verify 3:1 for marks and outlines. Every analysis offers 'View as table'.

principles.principle: Explain every number and show how assumptions move it. PAIR: explain data sources, favour partial explanations with progressive disclosure, beware confidence displays that backfire, prompt verification when stakes are high and confidence low. Forma's embodied-carbon analysis lets users view each scenario's data sources and customise them. Midwest Uncertainty Collective work supports quantile dotplots and outcome plots, but evidence is limited, so test locally. Carbon's status pattern wants colour plus symbol or shape plus text, and warns past five or six indicators.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Every metric opens 'Why this number?': formula, inputs, citation (title, link, retrieval date, section), status Sourced / Team assumption / FALSE ASSUMPTION, editable value with diff from default, change history. Status = colour plus icon plus word. Starting tokens (team assumption; contrast computed 21 Oct 2026, no colour-blind simulation yet): Sourced blue #1D5FBF light / #7FB2FF dark; Team assumption ochre #8A5A00 / #E3B341 with dashed outline; FALSE ASSUMPTION magenta #B0126F / #FF7AC6 with hatch, struck-through text and its own icon; each at least 5.4:1 on its theme's plates. Chips sit on opaque neutral plates, never directly on analysis colours. Where a result depends on editable assumptions, show a range band or quantile dots naming the drivers; pilot with 3-5 classmates. Chip cap per screen is an editable team assumption (Carbon's five or six). Flagged claims stay visible.

principles.principle: Make work reversible: undo, autosave, named snapshots and forkable files. NN/g lists undo and redo under user control. Figma autosaves checkpoints (every 30 minutes), lets users name versions, and restores without deleting anything. Speckle puts undo/redo in its status bar and saves views with camera, filters and sections. Rerun keeps layout apart from data and offers two reset levels. FME wires a visual Compare tool into git diff and merge; about three HN voices say visual programs are hard to diff or give to AI without a text form.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: One global undo stack spanning canvas, inspector and assumption edits. Continuous autosave; 'Save option' makes a named snapshot, which the Compare view needs. Restore adds a checkpoint and deletes nothing. Graph and module files are deterministic, key-sorted JSON so git diffs are readable; forks open a visual graph diff (added, removed, changed nodes and edited assumptions), planned after 10 Dec. Layouts and views are separate JSON from model data, with 'auto layout' and 'reset to my default'.

principles.principle: Compare options side by side, with linked views. Autodesk Forma's Compare mode shows up to six proposals or analysis results, syncs zoom and pan, and echoes point inspection in every pane (Autodesk quick-start page, opened via a regional mirror). NN/g comparison guidance: about five items, aligned attributes, sticky headers, highlight differences, hide identical attributes.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Compare view of named snapshots: one pane or column per option (up to six, compact layout above four; both numbers are editable guidance), aligned metric rows, sticky headers, 'show differences only', shared legends and scales, linked camera and linked point inspection on by default with an off switch (Forma precedent; whether Forma has a toggle is unverified), and PNG export of the compared view.

principles.principle: Notification restraint and ethical engagement. NN/g and Carbon: match interruption to urgency, prefer contextual indicators, never time out critical messages. deceptive.design lists 18 patterns (nagging, fake urgency, fake social proof, confirmshaming, addictive design). Gamification evidence is mixed in a secondary source that itself carries an unverified-text warning.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Default to no toasts; show run status inline on the node. Toasts only for non-critical events and auto-dismiss only when there is no action. No streaks, points, leaderboards, fake urgency or social proof, confirmshaming or nagging; use the deceptive.design list as a PR checklist. Community notifications are opt-in digests; analytics, if any, are opt-in. 'Progress' means evidence completeness, not a score; deadlines are shown factually.

principles.principle: Tokens, themes, type and motion from small sets. Linear generates themes in LCH from three variables (base, accent, contrast). OKLCH keeps lightness consistent but guarantees no contrast. NN/g: light mode generally reads better; offer dark as a user choice. NN/g animation: about 100-400 ms, around 100 ms for simple feedback, 200-300 ms for larger changes, 400 ms only for large moves; ease-out entering, ease-in exiting; parallax only with caution; honour reduced motion. Tailwind 4 reads tokens from CSS variables. Inter 4.1 has an opsz axis for Display sizes.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Tokens are CSS variables for 13 Nov, DTCG JSON through Style Dictionary v5 later. Neutral, accent and status scales come from three inputs in OKLCH plus a contrast control; light, dark and high-contrast by user choice; chrome low-chroma so analysis colours are the only saturated hues; viewport background themed separately. Durations 100, 200, 300 ms, 400 ms only for large panel moves; ease-out in, ease-in out; animate transform and opacity only; no bounce; no parallax (team decision); reducedMotion='user'. Inter variable with opsz plus Geist Mono, tabular figures, five type sizes.

principles.principle: WCAG 2.2 AA is reachable in a canvas tool only if wiring and viewport results get non-pointer and non-visual routes. React Flow documents keyboard focus, selection, node movement and edge deletion, not edge creation. WCAG's 2.1.1 Understanding page says connect-the-dots tasks, where only endpoints matter, need keyboard operation; 2.5.7 is met by click-click (connectOnClick). Precedents: IBM App Connect Toolkit's dialog with source and target terminal lists, Foblex f-flow v19 (C, arrows, Enter), Blender's Make Links (J) on selected nodes. 1.1.1: charts need short plus long alternatives and tables are recommended; Speckle's Elements dock is precedent.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: A 'Connect...' command on each focused port (also in Ctrl+K) opens a listbox of type-compatible target ports with type-ahead; an Edges list in the inspector with delete and rewire; click-click wiring and numeric inputs beside sliders; 24 px port hit areas or spacing; scroll-padding so panels never hide focus; 3:1 for ports, wires, focus rings and chart marks; 'View as table' (values per facade or zone) plus a long text summary for each viewport analysis; React Flow keyboard features on; axe-core in CI plus a manual keyboard and screen-reader pass.

principles.principle: Design Present mode around the competition's real constraints. Buildner terms: each panel is a JPEG of at most 10 MB, the brief sets one to four panels, judging is anonymous and marks that identify entrants are banned; the FAQ tells entrants to check AI tools' terms and not to treat AI images as sole work. The terms do not mention AI. A2 is 420 x 594 mm (4961 x 7016 px at 300 dpi, computed). Poster-type guidance comes from scientific-poster guides (UAB: 32 pt body on 36 x 48 in). OpenAI's image guide (read 21 Oct) caps outputs at 3840 px per edge and about 8.3 MP.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Board template on a 12-column grid (team assumption). Export profile: sRGB JPEG per panel; start at 300 dpi and step quality, then dpi, down until under 10 MB, showing the resulting size; strip identifying metadata. Type: body default 14 pt (UAB's 32 pt scaled by about 0.49 to A2), floors 10 pt body and 8 pt legends (team assumptions); preview at fit-to-screen (about 1080 px tall) because jurors may view panels that way. Charts are vector, rasterised at export, with units. Every AI image gets a visible caption 'AI-assisted image' with model and date, and the project logs prompt and model, since stripped metadata cannot carry provenance. Confirm the brief's AI wording first. Boards link to live model values and show a 'stale' badge after upstream edits.

principles.principle: Treat AI output as a labelled draft with provenance and a human in the loop. PAIR: explain data sources, show partial explanations, prompt verification in high-stakes low-confidence cases, show alternatives. Microsoft's HAX toolkit groups 18 guidelines into four phases (initially, during interaction, when wrong, over time); the list sits in a poster image I could not read. Buildner's FAQ warns that AI-generated images may not be the entrant's sole IP.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: AI-generated text, values and images carry an 'AI draft' label, show the inputs and sources used, and are editable. AI-suggested thresholds enter as Team assumption until a person attaches a source; never as Sourced. Show model name and version, keep prompts, make every AI action undoable, offer two or more alternatives for generated images, and never auto-apply AI edits to the graph.

recommendations.decision: Build the shell on Vite, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind 4.3 (CSS-first), shadcn ('init -t vite -b base') and MIT @xyflow/react 12.12 with our own node cards. Install Node LTS and pnpm first. Do not depend on React Flow UI templates; vendor a React Flow UI component only after xyflow confirms its licence, otherwise rewrite it.
recommendations.rationale: shadcn init defaults to Base UI since July 2026 with Radix still supported, so its docs, skill and registry items follow that path; the 11 React Flow UI registry files checked import no Radix package. Both React Flow UI templates are labelled Pro (from $169 per month) and use Next.js, ELKjs and Zustand. React Flow UI needs React 19 and Tailwind 4. Record the base in CLAUDE.md and PRODUCT.md, tell Claude to use 'render' not 'asChild', and pin versions.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: '-b radix' as default (kept as fallback; diverges from shadcn's default path); Pro templates (paid, Next.js, ELKjs); tldraw (production licence key); ComfyUI frontend and litegraph (GPL-3.0, archived); Rete.js (README showed no plugin detail); Blueprint or Carbon React (second visual system).

recommendations.decision: Keep Claude's design aids minimal: always the shadcn skill and MCP, plus one of the vendored Vercel checklist (default for 13 Nov) or Impeccable (after review, from 14 Nov). Use Anthropic's frontend-design only for Present-mode and landing pages. Do not install UI UX Pro Max. At most two aids per session.
recommendations.rationale: Five aids at once work against the token-saving goal and overlap context. Impeccable downloads an engine binary into ~/.impeccable/bin, writes hooks into .claude/settings.local.json that can trigger that download even if the launcher is denied, sends anonymous telemetry unless disabled, and its README lists Inter as overused. Review it with --no-hooks and DO_NOT_TRACK=1 first. Vercel's skill fetches rules from GitHub main, so vendor a pinned copy.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Installing every design skill together; unpinned Vercel fetch; Impeccable hooks on by default; UI UX Pro Max (MIT, 79 styles; overlaps and adds context, so dropped as a finding); Playwright MCP as the default review tool.

recommendations.decision: Make the phase journey a persistent, free-to-jump rail (Basic, Advanced, Present) with two disclosure levels per module, Essentials default on and everything in the command palette. Adopt an engagement-ethics policy: no streaks, points, leaderboards, fake urgency or social proof, nagging or confirmshaming; opt-in digests; inline status instead of toasts; 'progress' means evidence completeness.
recommendations.rationale: NN/g supports two-level progressive disclosure and says staged flows suit independent steps; our phases are interdependent. Figma and Linear keep focus on the canvas and avoid unstable hover UI. deceptive.design gives 18 named patterns; gamification evidence is mixed and the source read carries an unverified-text warning.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: A locked wizard; a Beginner mode that hides nodes (one ComfyUI commenter objected; evidence thin, so test before building); badges and XP for module uploads; countdown banners as pressure; push-style tours.

recommendations.decision: Write a node-canvas contract: typed ports (colour, shape, label), three wire modes, solid wires for the selected node, auto-framed categories, collapse-to-cluster, Tidy via dagre, named relays created with a modifier key, no implicit reconnection, hover inspection with units, a run-state taxonomy with stale propagation, click-click wiring, plus a keyboard 'Connect...' listbox and an Edges list.
recommendations.rationale: Wire clutter, organisation at scale and surprising implicit behaviour recur across McNeel, Blender, Hacker News and Unreal sources (informal coding of about 25 items; signals, not a study). WCAG 2.1.1 and 2.5.7 need keyboard and non-drag routes; React Flow documents neither keyboard edge creation, but IBM, Foblex and Blender provide precedents.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Free-form wiring without categories; drag-only connection; elkjs from day one (large); relying on React Flow's keyboard support alone; hiding wires by default (the McNeel thread is split); double-click relays.

recommendations.decision: Build one reusable SourceChip and 'Why this number?' panel with three statuses (Sourced, Team assumption, FALSE ASSUMPTION), tokens as in the starting values, each always paired with icon and word. AI-suggested values enter as Team assumption until a person attaches a source.
recommendations.rationale: PAIR advises explaining sources and favouring partial explanations; Carbon's status pattern pairs colour with symbol and text and caps indicators loosely; WCAG 1.4.1 forbids colour-only meaning; Forma's embodied-carbon analysis already exposes editable scenario data sources. Computed contrast for the starting hues is at least 5.4:1 on light and dark plates, but they differ little in luminance, so shape and words carry the meaning.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Footnote-only citations; colour-only flags; hiding falsified claims (the brief requires they stay visible); a FALSE ASSUMPTION hue shared with error red, warning amber or a data ramp end.

recommendations.decision: Create the token system in steps: CSS variables with Culori OKLCH scales for 13 Nov; DTCG JSON with Style Dictionary v5 later; Inter 4.1 (opsz) plus Geist Mono self-hosted from their repos; Crameri maps (MIT) for analysis colour; low-chroma chrome; Radix Colors only as a one-hour comparison.
recommendations.rationale: Linear shows three inputs can generate a whole theme; OKLCH gives consistent lightness; Crameri maps are uniform and colour-vision friendly, and Zenodo states MIT. Style Dictionary v5.7 supports DTCG but not fully the 2025.10 format. Tailwind 4 consumes CSS variables via '@theme inline'. Reserving saturation for data keeps results readable.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Hand-picked hex values; rainbow colour maps; Radix Colors and Culori in parallel; dark-only default; npm geist package (Next.js peer dependency); a tailwind.config.js theme.

recommendations.decision: Standardise results and options: Observable Plot with shared scales and always-visible legends, uncertainty bands where assumptions are editable, named option snapshots with global undo, a Compare view for up to six options with linked camera and linked point inspection, and 'View as table' for every analysis.
recommendations.rationale: Forma documents up to six compared results, synced views and inspect-in-all-panes; NN/g gives comparison rules; Carbon gives chart-anatomy rules; Figma and Speckle show snapshot and saved-view models; Plot's repo docs confirm legends from a scale definition. Snapshots are a prerequisite of Compare.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Single-number KPIs without ranges; per-chart auto-scaling that breaks cross-option comparison; hand-written SVG charts; a compare view without snapshots.

recommendations.decision: Make Present mode follow the competition: JPEG export profile under 10 MB per panel, anonymity-safe metadata, visible AI-image captions with a prompt log, and live-linked board values. Download the full brief yourselves and confirm panel count, A2, and AI wording; email organisers before the 3 Nov question deadline; registration closes 29 Oct.
recommendations.rationale: The Buildner terms set JPEG, 10 MB and anonymity, and the FAQ points to AI-tool terms; the brief PDF sits behind an email form that I did not submit. Stripping metadata for anonymity removes C2PA data, so provenance must live in captions and logs. Type sizes are scaled from a scientific-poster guide and are team assumptions.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Exporting 300 dpi PNG; relying on C2PA metadata for provenance (OpenAI's claim not opened directly); assuming four A2 panels; leaving AI images unlabelled.

recommendations.decision: Set quality gates: WCAG 2.2 AA, Playwright Test plus @axe-core/playwright in CI (pinned), the vendored Vercel checklist on changed UI files, Playwright MCP or pinned CLI for Claude's self-checks. Before 13 Nov run five 30-minute think-aloud sessions with Grasshopper-using classmates and a 3-task paper or Figma test of the phase rail and node card, then extend the complaint corpus.
recommendations.rationale: axe-core reports finding about 57% of WCAG issues; the aesthetic-usability effect can make a pretty UI look usable, so judge by task completion. The forum evidence gathered here is informal (McNeel, Blender, HN; Reddit blocked), so primary research is still needed.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Visual taste checks only; relying on Impeccable's detector alone (it targets AI-looking design, not WCAG); unpinned pre-1.0 @playwright/cli.

recommendations.decision: Sequence the UI work. By 13 Nov: shell and panels, CSS-variable tokens, canvas with typed ports, palette, one starter graph, SourceChip and 'Why this number?' panel, keyboard Connect, global undo. By 10 Dec: Compare with snapshots, uncertainty displays, table views, three starter graphs, motion, Present export profile, onboarding hints, CI accessibility, polish pass. Later: dockview, graph diff for forks, community theme tokens and module licence field, Yjs-based presence and comment pins, Speckle viewer extensions.
recommendations.rationale: Core items directly serve the module canvas, evidence and focus goals; polish and onboarding extras depend on stable components. Dates are the course deadlines supplied in the brief. Optional half-day Leva or Tweakpane spike in the v1 window.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Starting with Present-mode boards; building docking or community theming before the core canvas works; shipping all three starter graphs for 13 Nov.

flags.claim: tldraw is open source and can be embedded freely because it is on GitHub.
flags.correction: The SDK is under the tldraw licence: development free, production requires a licence key (trial or commercial; pricing page mentions a hobby licence whose terms were not read). Only the starter kits are MIT.
flags.detail: Sources: tldraw LICENSE.md, README, pricing page, all opened 21 Oct 2026. A public deployment counts as production. Confirmed again by the r1 critique.

flags.claim: ComfyUI's open-source node UI can be reused as code in our tool.
flags.correction: The frontend is GPL-3.0; copying code would force GPL on ours. litegraph.js (MIT) is archived. Use it as UX reference only.
flags.detail: Sources: GitHub API and README for Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_frontend and Comfy-Org/litegraph.js; docs page re-read in r1.

flags.claim: Radix is the default base under shadcn/ui; Base UI is only something to watch and its release status is unknown.
flags.detail: Since July 2026 'shadcn init' defaults to Base UI; Radix stays supported via '-b radix' (CLI also accepts 'aria'). Base UI is stable: npm @base-ui/react 1.9.0 (9 Oct 2026), MIT, 11.2k stars. Sources: ui.shadcn.com changelog 2026-07 and CLI docs, opened 21 Oct 2026; mui/base-ui README and npm registry.
flags.correction: Choose the base explicitly (this packet recommends Base UI via 'shadcn init -t vite -b base', with '-b radix' as fallback) and record it in CLAUDE.md and PRODUCT.md. React Flow UI registry items (11 checked) import no Radix package.

flags.claim: cmdk is limited to React 18.
flags.detail: cmdk 1.1.1 (14 Mar 2025) declares peerDependencies react ^18 || ^19 on the npm registry, read 21 Oct 2026.
flags.correction: cmdk supports React 19. The real risk is dormancy: no release since March 2025 and last push October 2025. kbar (timc1/kbar, MIT, npm 1.0.0, 10 Aug 2026) and React Aria are fallbacks behind our own Palette wrapper.

flags.claim: Whether Inter ships a Display cut is unresolved (the README says it is in the works).
flags.detail: Inter v4.0 (20 Nov 2023) release notes: six additional Display designs assigned to an opsz variable-font axis, exposed as a second family 'Inter Display' as static fonts. Current release v4.1 (16 Nov 2024). Source: GitHub releases API, read 21 Oct 2026.
flags.correction: Inter Display exists in Inter 4.x via the opsz axis; the README line is stale. Close the unresolved item.

flags.claim: React Flow's built-in keyboard support plus click-click wiring makes the canvas WCAG 2.2 AA-ready for wiring.
flags.detail: React Flow's accessibility and API docs (read 21 Oct 2026) describe Tab focus, Enter/Space selection, arrow-key node movement and edge deletion; connectOnClick (default true) covers single-pointer use (2.5.7). Neither documents creating edges from the keyboard. WCAG 2.1.1's Understanding page says connect-the-dots tasks, where only endpoints matter, need keyboard operation.
flags.correction: Build a keyboard 'Connect...' command with a type-compatible target listbox and an Edges list; precedents: IBM App Connect Toolkit dialog, Foblex f-flow v19, Blender Make Links (J). Add 'View as table' for viewport analyses (WCAG 1.1.1).

flags.claim: Crameri original maps have no stated licence (UNVERIFIED flag in round 0).
flags.detail: The Zenodo record for Scientific colour maps v8.0.1 (5 Oct 2023, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8409685) states the MIT License. Source: zenodo.org/records/8409685, opened 21 Oct 2026. The zip contents (66.9 MB) were not listed.
flags.correction: MIT. Bundle the colour stops with the MIT notice and cite Crameri et al. 2020 plus the DOI in the sources panel. The earlier UNVERIFIED flag is closed.

flags.claim: Linked cameras in the Compare view are an unsourced team assumption.
flags.detail: Autodesk's Forma quick-start guide (regional mirror www-pt.autodesk.com, opened 21 Oct 2026) describes Compare for up to six proposals or analysis results, zoom and pan updating all open scenes, and Inspect showing point details in every analysis. The autodesk.com tutorial page itself returned 403.
flags.correction: Cite Forma as precedent for linked cameras and linked point inspection. Whether linking can be switched off is not documented in pages read, so keep an off switch as our own design choice.

flags.claim: Style Dictionary activity and DTCG support are unknown; DTCG 2025.10 can be adopted through it.
flags.detail: npm shows style-dictionary 5.7.0 released 16 Oct 2026 (Apache-2.0). styledictionary.com/info/dtcg says DTCG is first-class since v4 and that full 2025.10 support is still in progress (planned for v5). Read 21 Oct 2026.
flags.correction: The project is active. Author tokens in the DTCG subset v5 supports and note the 2025.10 gaps; for 13 Nov keep plain CSS variables.

flags.claim: We can start from the React Flow UI Workflow Editor template (assumed free to adopt).
flags.detail: reactflow.dev/ui/templates/workflow-editor and /ai-workflow-editor both state 'This is a Pro example'; reactflow.dev/pro lists Starter at $169 per month with Pro examples and templates. The templates use Next.js, ELKjs, Zustand. No page states a licence for the free components; their registry JSON has no licence header. Opened 21 Oct 2026.
flags.correction: Do not plan on the templates. Build custom nodes on MIT @xyflow/react; treat individual registry components as references until xyflow confirms their licence.

flags.claim: Numeric UI thresholds in our rules are unsourced: seven Essentials per module, 3 significant figures, 200-node warning, six compared options (compact above four), status chips capped at five or six per screen, 12-column board grid, 14 pt body and 10 pt floors, 24 px ports beyond WCAG.
flags.detail: NN/g supports two disclosure levels and about five comparison items; Forma shows six compared results; Carbon only cautions about five or six indicators; type sizes are scaled from a scientific-poster guide. Mark all as editable team assumptions in the tool.

flags.claim: Starting colour tokens for Sourced, Team assumption and FALSE ASSUMPTION.
flags.detail: Hex values were chosen by us; WCAG contrast ratios were computed on 21 Oct 2026 (at least 5.4:1 on white, #F4F5F7, #16181C and #22252B). They have not been checked under colour-vision simulation, against every shipped Crameri ramp end, or in the viewport.

flags.claim: Base UI is the right shadcn base for our canvas, palette and popovers.
flags.detail: Chosen because it is shadcn's default and docs follow it. No side-by-side test with React Flow overlays and port popovers was run; Radix remains a '-b radix' fallback and shadcn offers a migration skill.

flags.claim: Interrupted work raises stress and cost (Mark et al., CHI 2008).
flags.detail: The ACM page returned 403 and the PDF was compressed binary I could not read; a fetch-tool summary recalled 'faster but more stressed' from memory. Do not cite as evidence until the paper is read.

flags.claim: Gamification improves learning outcomes (effect sizes reported in a Wikipedia article).
flags.detail: The article carries a banner about possibly unverified LLM-generated text; originals not checked. Evidence is mixed and structural gamification may not raise outcomes.

flags.claim: Blender socket inspection tooltips, the Viewer node and node timings behave as described.
flags.detail: Taken from a search-result summary of the Blender manual and tracker issue 85251; the manual body was not readable (navigation only). The Blender 'Make Links' (J) shortcut was read from the Editing Nodes manual page in r1.

flags.claim: Autodesk Forma legends, colour scales, units and uncertainty display, and whether camera linking can be turned off.
flags.detail: Compare behaviour (up to six, synced views, linked inspect) was read on a regional mirror of the quick-start guide and in Autodesk blogs, but autodesk.com tutorial pages return 403 and none of the pages read describe legends, units or uncertainty. No Forma trial was run.

flags.claim: Spline's editor is open source or has documented editor UX patterns we can cite.
flags.detail: Not confirmed. Only the Community Platform docs were opened (remix, repost, comments; community files CC BY 4.0). A search summary claiming CC0 was wrong. The interface-tour page was not opened.

flags.claim: GitHub star, issue and push-date figures.
flags.detail: Round 0 figures came through a summarising fetch tool and the API began returning 403 after about 45 calls. In r1 key repos (shadcn, xyflow, Impeccable, Base UI, Leva, Tweakpane, kbar, Yjs, Speckle, Culori, geist-font) were re-read from the unauthenticated GitHub API; the rest are unchanged. Spot-check before quoting numbers publicly.

flags.claim: React Flow UI component licence.
flags.detail: The site footer links xyflow's MIT licence but no page states a licence for the components; the registry JSON for base-node carries no licence header; templates are Pro. Ask xyflow (GitHub discussion or email) before vendoring any file.

flags.claim: Competition brief details: panel count, A2 size, resolution and any AI-imagery rule.
flags.detail: The terms say JPEG, 10 MB per panel, one to four panels per the brief, anonymous judging; they do not mention AI. The full brief PDF sits behind an email 'Get a link' form that I did not submit. Registration closes 29 Oct 2026 and the last day for questions is 3 Nov 2026.

flags.claim: OpenAI images carry C2PA metadata and an invisible SynthID watermark.
flags.detail: Only a search-result summary said so; OpenAI's help article returned 403 and the image-generation guide read in r1 says nothing about either. Do not rely on embedded provenance; use captions and a prompt log.

flags.claim: Impeccable's engine binary host, telemetry endpoint and hook behaviour are safe.
flags.detail: README says the binary downloads once into ~/.impeccable/bin, hooks write .claude/settings.local.json and can trigger the download, and a roll API at impeccable.style is called by default; the download URL is not named. Not inspected.

flags.claim: Node-editor praise and complaints from community sources.
flags.detail: Signals, not evidence: McNeel 48238 (16 posters) and 55455 (23 posters on the page read), one Blender DevTalk opening post (follow-up reads rate-limited), about 15 of 493 comments on one Hacker News thread. Reddit JSON and old.reddit returned 403; X, LinkedIn, YouTube, Discord not collected. Coding was informal.

unresolved: Competition brief (A2, panel count, resolution, AI rule): the PDF is behind an email form I did not submit. The team should download it and email organisers by 3 Nov 2026; registration closes 29 Oct 2026.
React Flow UI component licence (free components and Pro templates): no licence stated per component; ask xyflow before vendoring.

Social platforms: Reddit (JSON and old.reddit 403), X, LinkedIn, YouTube comments and Discord not collected. Hacker News (one thread, about 15 of 493 comments), McNeel (two threads) and one Blender DevTalk opening post were read; DevTalk follow-ups were rate-limited. A systematic 20-plus complaint corpus is not done.
Primary user research with ARCH 540 students and Grasshopper users has not happened; it needs the team (five 30-minute sessions plus a 3-task test of the phase rail and node card).
Autodesk Forma: autodesk.com tutorials return 403; legends, colour scales, units, uncertainty display and whether camera linking toggles are not documented in pages read; no trial run.
Blender node editor conventions (socket inspection, Viewer node, node timings): manual pages too large to read; only Make Links (J) and Mute Links were confirmed.
OpenAI C2PA and SynthID provenance claims: help article 403, image guide silent; secondary sources only.
Impeccable engine binary host and telemetry endpoint not named in the README and not inspected.
Base UI versus Radix not tested side by side with canvas overlays, port popovers and the palette; shadcn's Command docs do not explain base differences.
Spline editor UX and licence: only the Community Platform docs opened; interface tour not read.
Speckle: Viewer 3 features, legends and themes not verified; docs conflict on who can create saved views (Editor seat versus Contributor role).
tldraw hobby-licence terms and any educational or open-source exemption: not fetched.
Licences not stated or not checked: React Flow UI components, DTCG, deceptive.design content, Crameri JavaScript packaging (zip contents), W3C document licence.
Microsoft HAX Toolkit's 18 guidelines (poster image unreadable) and the Mark et al. CHI 2008 paper and Cognitive Dimensions tutorial (binary PDFs) were not read.
Print and type guidance for A2 comes only from scientific-poster guides (UAB, scaled); no architecture-competition source found, and jurors may view panels on screen.
Collaboration and presence UX (Yjs: MIT on npm, NOASSERTION on GitHub) for team comments on nodes: not researched.
Tweakpane README and Leva scrub/typed-input behaviour not verified; spike needed.
Laws of UX numbers (for example Miller's 7 plus or minus 2) were deliberately not used as rules; no primary source read.
change_log: r1: Replaced the Radix finding with a combined 'Base UI (new shadcn default) and Radix Primitives' finding; shadcn init now defaults to Base UI (July 2026), Radix via -b radix; recommended 'shadcn init -t vite -b base' and recording the choice. Added FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag.

r1: React Flow UI downgraded from core to v1: both templates are labelled Pro (from $169 per month), component licences are unstated, registry files carry no licence header; 11 components checked import no Radix. Added FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag for the template assumption and kept the UNRESOLVED licence flag.

r1: Added keyboard edge creation and viewport table alternatives to the WCAG plan (principle 13, React Flow finding); evidence from React Flow docs, WCAG 2.1.1 and 1.1.1 Understanding pages, IBM, Foblex f-flow v19 and Blender Make Links. Added FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag.

r1: Added benchmark cards for Autodesk Forma (compare evidence read on a regional Autodesk mirror and blogs), Figma UI3, Linear, Speckle (viewer UX docs), Spline (community remix, CC BY 4.0), Rerun and Observable Plot; promoted linked cameras from team assumption to sourced (FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag).

r1: Added principles for reversibility (undo, autosave, snapshots, graph diff), node run states and error copy, units and precision, Present mode and A2 boards, and AI-assistance UX; merged earlier principles to stay at 15 (disclosure with chrome-recedes, explainability with uncertainty, tokens with motion).

r1: Rewrote the wires principle with informal forum evidence (McNeel 48238 and 55455, a Blender DevTalk proposal, one HN thread); the wire default is now a three-mode switch decided by testing, relays need a modifier key, no implicit reconnection. Evidence labelled as signals; Reddit remained blocked.

r1: Vancouver Tall Challenge page and terms opened: JPEG panels up to 10 MB, anonymity, FAQ on AI tools, dates (registration 29 Oct, questions 3 Nov). Brief PDF is behind an email form I did not submit; A2 and AI rule remain unresolved. Added Present-mode export profile and AI caption rules.

r1: Narrowed the 13 Nov core (one starter graph, shell, tokens, canvas, palette, SourceChip, keyboard Connect, undo); limited design aids to two per session; Impeccable moved to v1 with a review step (telemetry on by default, binary download, hooks, Inter flagged); UI UX Pro Max dropped as a finding.

r1: Factual corrections applied: cmdk supports React 19 (risk is dormancy); Inter 4.x has Display via opsz and v4.1 is current; Crameri maps are MIT (Zenodo 8409685); Style Dictionary v5.7.0 with first-class DTCG and incomplete 2025.10 support; Tailwind 4 CSS-first with @theme inline; Playwright CLI pre-1.0 pinned; Geist Mono taken from the geist-font repo (npm package is a Next.js peer); status indicator needs colour, icon and text with the chip cap as an editable team assumption; NN/g motion durations restated as 100-400 ms.

r1: Added concrete status tokens (blue, ochre, magenta with hatch) with computed contrast of at least 5.4:1 on four plates; flagged as team assumptions pending colour-vision simulation and a check against shipped ramp ends.
r1: Added Leva and Tweakpane as a half-day parameter-panel spike; dockview folded into the panels finding; Yjs presence noted as roadmap and unresolved.

r1: To stay within 30 findings, folded Radix Colors into the Culori finding, d3-scale-chromatic into Observable Plot, React Aria into cmdk, axe-core into the Playwright finding, and dropped Driver.js (kept as an optional library in the onboarding rule) and UI UX Pro Max as separate findings.

r1: Closed the round-0 UNVERIFIED flag on Crameri licensing (replaced by FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag) and revised the UNVERIFIED Forma and Spline flags and the TEAM_ASSUMPTION flag; earlier FALSE_ASSUMPTION flags were kept.
